maya: Noticing syscall tail on small-stream traffic after recent ingress change. dropping notes.

maya: baseline small-stream p95 host-parse ~190ms, seen ~340ms on canary.

maya: perf-sample top deltas: memcpy +14%, grpc_writev/readv +120%, parse_tokenize +18%.

todd: Sounds like per-request linearize + extra writev. Which change?

maya: We added a prebatch probe that copies fragments into a temp buffer to estimate density and pick packed kernel. That probe does a malloc+memcpy per request before batching.

sam: So for N small reqs we do N probes (malloc+memcpy) then batcher merges -> another copy. Double work. Also more small syscalls when streaming replies.

bench-bot: canary quick metrics: host-parse CPU +17%, allocs/sec +35%, syscall rate (writev) +210%, small-stream p95 +75%.

todd: Short fixes: 1) rollback probe rule on canary (quick) 2) implement per-worker slab of prealigned scratch buffers (avoid malloc) 3) postpone probe/selection until after batching so we probe once per batch.

maya: Agreed. I'll open revert PR and a sticky-slab PR behind feature flag. Also will add telemetry: kernel_phase={prebatch,postbatch}, scratch_slab_hit=true/false, ingress_coalesce=true/false, grpc_syscall_count.

sam: For ingress coalesce: prototype buffering small outgoing frames up to 4KB or 2ms and emit a single writev. That should reduce syscall tail. Flag it as ingress.coalesce. Watch latency impact on p50.

infra-bot: rollback PR deployed to canary at 09:22 UTC. Monitoring: host-parse p95 and syscall_rate.

maya: Post-rollback quick numbers (09:40): memcpy share down to ~3%, syscall rate back to baseline, host-parse p95 ~200ms. Revert fixed immediate regression.

todd: Next: land slab + coalescer experiments on 5% canary, run microbench replay: baseline, bad-probe, slab-only, slab+coalesce, postbatch-select. Measure p50/p95, memcpy time, allocs/sec, grpc_syscall_count, kvcache_hit_rate.

maya: I'll attach the replay script and a flame to the slab ticket (RTX-7001). Please tag dashboards.

sam: Long-term: kernel should accept iovecs/segments to avoid copies entirely (RTX-7002). For now, slab + coalesce + postbatch-select are our path.

bench-bot: microbench queued: replay/403210-001. ETA ~30m.

maya: Thanks team. Fast detection + rollback. Will post results here.
